sections.h2: What are my options to sell a house in Carrollton, TX?
sections.html:
In Carrollton, a seller can hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or sell straight to a cash buyer. A cash sale trades a lower price for speed and fewer repairs, and a listing trades time for a higher possible price. Pick by looking at repairs, liens and your moving date.

One Carrollton quirk comes first: the city sits in parts of Dallas, Denton and Collin counties. Your property tax bill, appraisal district and recording office all follow the county your lot is in, so confirm that on your tax statement before you start.

sections.h2: What is Carrollton like for a seller?
sections.html:
Carrollton is described by its own city site as a centrally located city in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. It has three DART light rail stations, including Downtown Carrollton Station on the Silver Line, and is served by IH-35E, SH 121 and the President George Bush Turnpike. Dallas Love Field and DFW International Airport are both within driving distance.

  • Rail access helps houses near stations that appeal to commuters.
  • The city lists sports complexes, hike and bike trails, a nature preserve and the Rosemeade Rainforest Aquatic Complex among its amenities.
  • Carrollton-Farmers Branch ISD is the school district named in the city's history pages, and its oldest school, Carrollton High School, opened in 1936.
  • The city's Festival at the Switchyard is its fall signature event.

Buyers often ask about commute time, school zoning and flood history, so have those answers ready.

Carrollton incorporated on June 14, 1913, by a 52 to 23 vote, per a city marker described on its historical designations page. The settlement grew around railroads, and the Town Square still has early 20th century buildings. Brick made in town went into homes such as a 1910 prairie-style house on Clint Street, and the city's page records a brick company that supplied the early school.

That legacy means older core neighborhoods hold houses from several eras, and a house near the Elm Fork or old creek beds may carry flood history. The city's historical page notes floods in 1908, the 1920s and the 1940s at a house near Belt Line Road. If your house sits in a low area, a buyer may ask for flood insurance quotes, so gather any claims history.

Not for new operators. Carrollton passed Zoning Ordinance 4297 and Code Ordinance 4291 on December 2, 2025, and its Environmental Services page says no new short-term rental or bed and breakfast will be allowed. Only certain existing properties can qualify for a lodging license under Chapter 97 of the city code.

Carrollton short-term rental requirements for existing operators
RequirementWhat the city says
Lodging licenseNeeded every year for each location
Ownership changeA new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought
Hotel occupancy taxRequired of all short-term rentals
Other rulesChapter 97, the zoning ordinance and other city codes apply

Source: City of Carrollton, Short Term Rental and Bed and Breakfast. Because a license belongs to a specific owner and location, a house that runs as a rental today may not be able to keep that use for a buyer. Disclose that early, and call Environmental Services at (972) 466-3060 for the status of your address.

sections.h2: How do taxes work for Carrollton homeowners?
sections.html:
Because of the three counties, the appraisal district and tax assessor differ by parcel. The common rules come from the state: values are set January 1, the lien for that year's tax attaches the same day, and most bills are due by January 31 of the next year.

  • School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption; owners who are 65 or older or disabled receive an extra $60,000.
  • The school tax on a qualifying senior or disabled homestead is capped at the level set when the owner first qualified.
  • Homestead appraisals are limited to a 10 percent annual increase, with exceptions for new additions.
  • Protest filing is generally by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later.

Ask the county that bills your parcel for a payoff figure and whether an installment plan exists on any delinquent balance.

sections.h2: How are a Carrollton house sale and deed recorded?
sections.html:
The county clerk for your lot's county takes the deed, whether that is Dallas, Denton or Collin. A general warranty deed, special warranty deed or quitclaim deed is accepted if it is signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer such as a notary.

The Texas courts' 2023 clerk manual lists a $5.00 first-page fee and $4.00 for each added page, plus other clerk fees that vary by county. A title company usually pays those at closing and files for you. If an old tax lien or a mechanic's lien appears, it must be cleared before a buyer can get clear title.

sections.h2: What if a Carrollton house is inherited or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
For inherited property, check whether the estate used a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration, since each leaves different paperwork for the county clerk. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement that no court has verified, and no law makes a buyer or title company accept it.

For a loan in default, the servicer gives 20 days to reinstate and posts a notice of sale at least 21 days ahead of a first-Tuesday auction. A deficiency suit must be filed within two years of the sale. Selling before the auction date can keep equity that would otherwise be eaten by costs.

sections.h2: What if Carrollton property taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax becomes a larger problem every month. The Comptroller says a six percent penalty and one percent interest attach on February 1, the penalty continues at one percent a month until July 1, and then reaches 12 percent. Interest has no ceiling, and a lawyer retained by the taxing unit can add up to 20 percent.

  • Collectors may offer installment plans on delinquent tax, up to 36 months in some cases, and a plan is required for a residence homestead.
  • A tax lien lets the unit sue to foreclose even if the owner changes, so unpaid tax must be paid off at or before closing.
  • If a house is sold at a tax sale, owners of homestead property can redeem it for two years from the date the purchaser's deed is filed, with a premium that the Supreme Court of Texas opinion describes as 25 percent in the first year and 50 percent in the second.
  • Excess proceeds from a tax sale can be claimed by the former owner within two years of the sale.

Ask the tax office of the county that bills your Carrollton lot for the payoff before you accept any offer.

faqs.q: Which county is my Carrollton house in?
faqs.a: It could be Dallas, Denton or Collin. The city lies in parts of all three. Look at your tax bill or the county appraisal district map, because that decides where taxes are paid and the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I start a new short-term rental in Carrollton?
faqs.a: No. Ordinances passed December 2, 2025 say no new short-term rental or bed and breakfast will be allowed, with only certain existing properties able to qualify for a lodging license. Call the city before assuming any rental use can continue.

faqs.q: Does a Carrollton lodging license pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. Licenses belong to the specific owner and location, and a change in ownership means a new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought. A buyer should not rely on the seller's license.

faqs.q: How much homestead exemption do Carrollton schools give?
faqs.a: School districts must give $140,000 on a residence homestead, plus $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Cities and counties may add local exemptions, so ask your county for the current list.

faqs.q: Can Carrollton heirs sell without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A small estate affidavit works for qualifying estates, and a muniment of title can follow a court order. Without one of those routes, title may be hard to clear, so speak to the county clerk or a probate attorney.
